title: Mutual Linearity of Complexes in Chemical Reaction Networks
authors: Pedro E. Harunari, Guilherme Fiusa, Matteo Polettini
abstract: Exact statements about how a system far from equilibrium responds to changes in its rate constants are scarce beyond linear response, yet they are central to the control of biochemical networks. A notable exception is mutual linearity: in a jump process, controlling the rates of a single transition makes any two stationary probabilities obey an exact affine relation, arbitrarily far from equilibrium. With nonlinear mass-action kinetics, and conservation laws in place of a normalization, chemical reaction networks seem to defy mutual linearity since species concentrations obey no such relation. We show that it was there all along, in the complexes' activities (mass-action monomials) rather than in the concentrations of species. For zero-deficiency networks with a single linkage class, controlling one reaction makes any three stationary activities obey a linear relation whose coefficients are independent of the controlled rate constants, the conserved quantities (hence the initial state), and even of the stoichiometry of complexes. This predicts hidden activities and bounds the activity ratios the control can reach, while a violation signals nonzero deficiency or multiple linkage classes.
summary: This work establishes a powerful structural property called 'mutual linearity' for the activities of complexes in chemical reaction networks. It proves that this linearity holds exactly, even far from equilibrium, provided the network has zero deficiency. This relationship serves as a powerful diagnostic tool, as its violation signals structural flaws like non-zero deficiency.
main_problem: The paper investigates finding exact, non-linear relationships (mutual linearity) describing how a system far from equilibrium responds to changes in its reaction rate constants.
main_result: Mutual linearity holds not for species concentrations, but for the activities of the reaction complexes ($\psi_c$), yielding a three-term linear relation independent of the controlled rate constants.
method: The proof utilizes concepts from Markov chain theory, specifically analyzing the coplanarity of spanning-tree polynomials derived from the complex-space Laplacian.
model_or_system: The system is Chemical Reaction Networks (CRNs) operating under mass-action kinetics, analyzed in the context of jump processes and complex-balance equations.
key_observables: Stationary activities of complexes ($\psi_c$), which are mass-action monomials; the relationship $\Delta_{bc}\psi_a + \Delta_{ca}\psi_b + \Delta_{ab}\psi_c = 0$.
important_parameters: Zero deficiency ($\delta=0$) and the condition of having a single linkage class are crucial structural requirements for the theorem to hold.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the network is zero-deficiency and that the controlled reaction is bidirectional and not a bridge.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the theorem using a Michaelis-Menten cycle, showing the linear collapse of the mutual linearity product. Figure 2 demonstrates the relation holding for a complex network and its violation when the deficiency increases.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem of non-equilibrium response, proves the existence of mutual linearity in complex activities for specific network structures, derives the general linear relation, and uses this relation to test structural invariants like network deficiency.
why_interesting: While focused on classical chemical kinetics, the mathematical machinery—relating structural invariants (deficiency) to algebraic constraints (linearity)—is highly relevant to understanding constraints in open quantum systems or quantum field theories where non-equilibrium steady states are studied.
